verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "I've been having a cough and a sore throat for about a week".
Patient says: "The sore throat came first and then after day or two, the cough."
Patient reports SOB started "shortly after the cough... maybe a day or two later. So three, four days ago?"
Doctor asks: "do you have any wheeze or chest pain?" Patient replies "Yeah." Doctor confirms: "You'Re feeling a bit wheezy..."
Doctor initially: "do you have any wheeze or chest pain?" Patient: "Yeah." Later doctor clarifies: "And you say you don't have any chest pain as such." Thus chest pain is ultimately denied.
Doctor: "is the cough worse at nighttime?" Patient: "No, it's the same throughout the day. Same throughout the day."
Doctor: "are you coughing up anything?" Patient: "No, it's very dry." and later: "It's a dry cough. No. You're not coughing up any phlegm."
Doctor: "you're not coughing up blood or anything like that?" Patient: "No, no."
Doctor: "are you feeling feverish?" Patient: "a little bit feverish at first, so the first three or so days of this, but then the fever's gone away."
Patient: "also had a bit of a headache, like headaches that come and go rather. But like, right now it's fine."
Patient: "I have been losing my appetite recently... that's been a bit concerning."
Doctor: "you haven't lost any weight that you think of?" Patient: "No, not that."
Doctor: "you say you have a cold, so do you have sinus congestion or." Patient: "No, it seems to be almost entirely with just my throat."
Patient says symptoms are "almost entirely with just my throat" but also reports cough and shortness of breath; thus not throat only.
Doctor: "do you have any other medical conditions or medical history?" Patient: "No just. No past medical history? No."
Doctor: "Are you allergic to any medications?" Patient: "Not to any medication, but I'm allergic to peanuts."
Patient: "Well, my mother had lung cancer." Doctor repeats: "Your mother had lung cancer."
Patient: "I was born in the US and moved over about 12 years ago..." and they are currently consulting a UK GP service.
Doctor: "Do you smoke?" Patient: "No... I mean, once or twice in Amsterdam, but not really." This indicates occasional smoking.
Doctor considers examination: "I don't know if I could sort of look inside your throat..." then: "Oh, we can try. Oh, no, well, no, it's okay." So no visual throat exam was performed.
Doctor: "Have you got any lumps or bumps around your neck that you can feel?" Patient: "No, not the. No."
History includes sore throat and dry cough for a week, initial fever for first three days, and headaches that come and go; consistent with an acute upper respiratory infection.
Shortness of breath and wheeze are reported, but chest pain is ultimately denied: "you say you don't have any chest pain as such." Non‑exertional nature is never specified.
Patient: "have been losing my appetite recently" and later confirms no weight loss: "you haven't lost any weight..." "No, not that."
Doctor advises: "paracetamol, lots of fluids, and rest up."
Doctor provides reassurance about cancer and TB and says: "if you're not feeling better, please get in touch" and to seek care if significantly worse.
Doctor: "I'll provide you with a sick note just to give you a few more days off work."
Doctor: "expect this to sort of be getting better in the next four or five days. If it's not, please get in touch with the medical professional again" and also advises follow‑up if symptoms worsen.
